{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01NbVrLhdVcxQBZwbeKA8o21","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# Prime DataQ Health, LLC — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-15\n     4→Developer website: https://www.summitehr.com/\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→Prime DataQ Health, LLC is the formal entity behind **DataQ Health**, a healthcare technology and clinical services company headquartered in Dallas, Texas. Founded in 2020 by Dr. R. Haris Naseem (a cardiac electrophysiologist who has founded 10+ healthcare ventures), DataQ Health initially focused on population health management, value-based care services, and MIPS reporting. In 2023, DataQ acquired Wiseman Innovations, LLC, a healthcare data analytics and population health management company, to strengthen its analytics and predictive modeling capabilities.\n     9→\n    10→DataQ Health developed its **360 Platform** suite — including 360 DeepLearn™ (risk stratification), 360 CareManager™ (care coordination), 360 Ribbon™ (EMR integration), and related tools — aimed at ACOs and value-based care organizations. The company reports serving 15,000 providers across 3,000 practices with $295M in total shared savings, though these figures likely relate to its population health/MIPS business, not the EHR product.\n    11→\n    12→**summitEHR** is a newer product, a joint venture between DataQ Health and **Summus Health Care** — a North Texas healthcare management and services organization also founded by Dr. Naseem. Summus Healthcare operates 35+ primary care and specialty providers across the Dallas-Fort Worth area through entities including Premier Independent Physicians (primary care/internal medicine network), North Texas Diabetes & Endocrinology, Premier Care Behavioral Health, and Starwood Pharmacy. The summitEHR product was certified on August 27, 2025, making it a very recent entrant to the certified EHR market.\n    13→\n    14→DataQ Health appears to be a small company. No public funding rounds, revenue figures, or significant employee counts were found. The company is privately held and does not appear in major EHR market rankings or third-party review platforms (G2, Capterra, KLAS, etc.). No independent user reviews of summitEHR were found on any review platform.\n    15→\n    16→## Product: summitEHR\n    17→\n    18→CHPL ID: 11689\n    19→CHPL Product Number: 15.04.04.3236.Davi.01.00.1.250827\n    20→Version: 1.0\n    21→Certified: 2025-08-27\n    22→\n    23→### What It Is\n    24→\n    25→summitEHR is an ambulatory electronic health record system designed for internal medicine, endocrinology, and cardiology specialties (per the SED intended user description). The vendor markets it more broadly as suitable for primary care practices, multispecialty groups, and behavioral health providers.\n    26→\n    27→The product was certified against a broad set of 34 ONC criteria spanning clinical data management (a)(1)–(a)(5), (a)(12), (a)(14)–(a)(15); transitions of care (b)(1)–(b)(3); clinical quality measures (c)(1)–(c)(3); patient portal/view-download-transmit (e)(1); FHIR APIs (g)(7), (g)(9)–(g)(10); direct messaging (h)(1); and the full suite of security/infrastructure criteria (d)(1)–(d)(9), (d)(12)–(d)(13). This is a comprehensive ambulatory EHR certification profile.\n    28→\n    29→The product tagline is \"Designed by clinicians, deployed in weeks,\" emphasizing quick onboarding and clinical workflow alignment. The vendor describes it as a \"modern platform built for connected, value-based care\" with embedded AI and predictive modeling capabilities — reflecting DataQ Health's existing analytics background.\n    30→\n    31→### Users & Market\n    32→\n    33→**Target users**: Physicians, clinical staff, and practice administrators in ambulatory settings — specifically internal medicine, endocrinology, and cardiology, though the marketing also mentions behavioral health and primary care.\n    34→\n    35→**Customer base**: Unknown. No customer counts, case studies, or testimonials specific to summitEHR were found. Given the very recent certification date (August 2025) and the version number (1.0), it's likely that the product is in early deployment stages. Summus Healthcare's own network (35+ providers in DFW) is the most probable initial/anchor customer, as the product was explicitly co-developed between DataQ Health and Summus Health Care.\n    36→\n    37→**Market position**: Very small, very new. summitEHR does not appear on any third-party EHR comparison sites, review platforms, or market analyses. No press coverage beyond the vendor's own website was found. This is essentially a startup EHR.\n    38→\n    39→**Deployment model**: Appears to be cloud-hosted based on the web-based interface and \"deployed in weeks\" messaging, though this is not explicitly stated.\n    40→\n    41→### Modules & Functionality\n    42→\n    43→Based on the vendor website (summitehr.com) and the ONC certification page, summitEHR includes the following capabilities:\n Haris Naseem (a cardiac electrophysiologist who has founded 10+ healthcare ventures), DataQ Health initially focused on population health management, value-based care services, and MIPS reporting. In 2023, DataQ acquired Wiseman Innovations, LLC, a healthcare data analytics and population health management company, to strengthen its analytics and predictive modeling capabilities.\n\nDataQ Health developed its **360 Platform** suite — including 360 DeepLearn™ (risk stratification), 360 CareManager™ (care coordination), 360 Ribbon™ (EMR integration), and related tools — aimed at ACOs and value-based care organizations. The company reports serving 15,000 providers across 3,000 practices with $295M in total shared savings, though these figures likely relate to its population health/MIPS business, not the EHR product.\n\n**summitEHR** is a newer product, a joint venture between DataQ Health and **Summus Health Care** — a North Texas healthcare management and services organization also founded by Dr. Naseem. The summitEHR product was certified on August 27, 2025, making it a very recent entrant to the certified EHR market.\n\nDataQ Health appears to be a small company. No independent user reviews of summitEHR were found on any review platform.\n\n## Product: summitEHR\n\nCHPL ID: 11689\nCHPL Product Number: 15.04.04.3236.Davi.01.00.1.250827\nVersion: 1.0\nCertified: 2025-08-27\n\n### What It Is\n\nsummitEHR is an ambulatory electronic health record system designed for internal medicine, endocrinology, and cardiology specialties (per the SED intended user description). The vendor markets it more broadly as suitable for primary care practices, multispecialty groups, and behavioral health providers.\n\nThe product was certified against a broad set of 34 ONC criteria spanning clinical data management (a)(1)–(a)(5), (a)(12), (a)(14)–(a)(15); transitions of care (b)(1)–(b)(3); clinical quality measures (c)(1)–(c)(3); patient portal/view-download-transmit (e)(1); FHIR APIs (g)(7), (g)(9)–(g)(10); direct messaging (h)(1); and the full suite of security/infrastructure criteria (d)(1)–(d)(9), (d)(12)–(d)(13). This is a comprehensive ambulatory EHR certification profile.\n\nThe product tagline is \"Designed by clinicians, deployed in weeks,\" emphasizing quick onboarding and clinical workflow alignment. The vendor describes it as a \"modern platform built for connected, value-based care\" with embedded AI and predictive modeling capabilities — reflecting DataQ Health's existing analytics background.\n\n### Users & Market\n\n**Target users**: Physicians, clinical staff, and practice administrators in ambulatory settings — specifically internal medicine, endocrinology, and cardiology, though the marketing also mentions behavioral health and primary care.\n\n**Customer base**: Unknown. No customer counts, case studies, or testimonials specific to summitEHR were found. Given the very recent certification date (August 2025) and the version number (1.0), it's likely that the product is in early deployment stages. Summus Healthcare's own network (35+ providers in DFW) is the most probable initial/anchor customer, as the product was explicitly co-developed between DataQ Health and Summus Health Care.\n\n**Market position**: Very small, very new. summitEHR does not appear on any third-party EHR comparison sites, review platforms, or market analyses. No press coverage beyond the vendor's own website was found. This is essentially a startup EHR.\n\n**Deployment model**: Appears to be cloud-hosted based on the web-based interface and \"deployed in weeks\" messaging, though this is not explicitly stated.\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nBased on the vendor website (summitehr.com) and the ONC certification page, summitEHR includes the following capabilities:\n\n**Clinical Documentation**\n- Smart templates and voice-enabled charting\n- Quick actions and streamlined note completion\n- Auto-coding assistance (AI-powered suggestions for coding)\n- The (a)(1)–(a)(5) certifications confirm: CPOE for medications, labs, and diagnostic imaging; demographics; problem list; medication list; medication allergy list\n\n**Electronic Prescribing**\n- Real-time pharmacy connectivity (electronic prescription routing)\n- Medication history access (view past prescriptions and fill history)\n- Drug interaction alerts (allergies, interactions, dosage issues)\n- EPCS (Electronic Prescribing of Controlled Substances) compliance\n- Integrates with **NewCrop** for e-prescribing (noted on the ONC certification page)\n\n**Patient Management**\n- Integrated scheduling with appointment reminders\n- Secure messaging between providers and patients\n- Telehealth capabilities built into the platform\n\n**Patient Portal**\n- Certified for (e)(1) — view, download, and transmit health information\n- Patient access to their records\n\n**Care Coordination**\n- Team-based workflows with task delegation\n- Transparent communication tools across practices\n- Certified for transitions of care (b)(1)–(b)(3) — create, receive, and reconcile C-CDAs\n- Direct messaging via **EMR Direct** integration (noted on ONC certification page)\n\n**Analytics & Reporting**\n- Dashboards tracking quality metrics and financial performance\n- Population health trend analysis\n- Predictive analytics for risk identification\n- Clinical quality measure reporting — certified for (c)(1)–(c)(3) — CQM capture, export, and reporting\n- 13 clinical quality measures tested per the ONC certification page\n\n**Interoperability**\n- FHIR API access — certified for (g)(7), (g)(9), (g)(10)\n- Connections with labs, pharmacies, HIEs, and payers\n- Direct messaging for clinical information exchange (h)(1)\n- OAuth 2.0 authentication\n\n**Security**\n- Optional multi-factor authentication (MFA)\n- End-user device encryption\n- Trusted connection protocols\n- Full suite of (d) criteria: authentication, auditing, authorization, encryption, etc.\n\n**Implantable Device List**\n- Certified for (a)(14) — maintaining a list of a patient's implantable devices\n\n**Social/Psychological/Behavioral Data**\n- Certified for (a)(15) — capturing social, psychological, and behavioral data\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on the certified criteria and described features, summitEHR stores and manages:\n\n- **Patient demographics** — (a)(5) certification\n- **Problem lists** — (a)(3) certification\n- **Medication lists** — (a)(4) certification, plus e-prescribing data via NewCrop integration\n- **Medication allergy lists** — (a)(2) certification\n- **Clinical notes** — voice-enabled charting, smart templates\n- **Orders** — CPOE for medications (a)(1), labs (a)(12), and diagnostic imaging (a)(12 context suggests lab/radiology ordering)\n- **Prescription data** — e-prescribing with EPCS, medication history, pharmacy connectivity\n- **Lab results** — interoperability with labs, (b)(11) certification for electronic health information export\n- **Clinical quality measure data** — (c)(1)–(c)(3) certified\n- **Implantable device data** — (a)(14) certified\n- **Social/psychological/behavioral data** — (a)(15) certified\n- **Care plans and transition of care documents** — (b)(1)–(b)(3) certified, C-CDA generation\n- **Patient portal messages** — secure messaging described\n- **Scheduling/appointment data** — integrated scheduling with reminders\n- **Telehealth session data** — telehealth built into the platform\n- **Audit logs** — (d)(2) certified\n- **Direct messages** — (h)(1) certified, EMR Direct integration\n\n**What's unclear or absent:**\n- **Billing/claims**: The website does not explicitly describe billing, claims management, or revenue cycle management as a feature. The mention of \"financial performance dashboards\" and \"auto-coding assistance\" hints at some billing-adjacent functionality, but it's unclear whether summitEHR includes integrated billing or if billing is handled externally. This is a notable gap in the available information.\n- **Document management/scanning**: No mention of document imaging or scanning capabilities.\n- **Patient-reported outcomes**: Not mentioned.\n- **Faxing**: Not mentioned, though this is common in ambulatory EHRs.\n- **Referral management**: Not explicitly described, though care coordination is mentioned.\n- **Practice management**: The product emphasizes clinical workflows; it's unclear whether practice management (insurance verification, eligibility checking, claims submission) is built in or separate.\n","numLines":127,"startLine":1,"totalLines":127}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01NwxraW3MLRjSYwZJzBMxh6","type":"tool_result","content":"EHI Export Documentation\nSummitEHR (v1.0)\n\n\fUnderstanding TSV (Tab-Separated Values)\nThe exported data is provided in a machine-readable TSV (Tab-Separated Values) format, making it easy to\nopen, process, or share. Each record (or row) in the file is represented on a separate line, and the fields (or\ncolumns) within each record are separated by tab (\\t) characters. This format is widely used for data\nexchange due to its simplicity and compatibility.\nSummitEHR’s EHI Export feature lets you manually export a patient's complete health record - or the full\npatient population for a practice.\nTo support bulk export of Electronic Health Information (EHI) across multiple patients, SummitEHR\ngenerates a separate TSV file for each type of resource. Within a resource file, each row within a file contains\ndata for a single patient.\n\nPrograms to Open or View TSV Files\nTSV files can be opened using a variety of programs, including:\n\n\n\n\n\nMicrosoft Excel – Opens TSV files and arranges data in tabular format automatically.\nGoogle Sheets – Supports TSV upload and allows for online viewing and editing.\nNotepad / Notepad++ – Text editors that allow manual inspection of the raw tab-separated data.\nPython / R / Data Analysis Tools – Developers can use programming libraries (like Pandas in Python)\nto parse and manipulate TSV data.\n\nStructure of TSV Files\nEach TSV file includes:\n\n\n\n\nA header row that names each column\nSubsequent rows for each data record\nFields separated by tab characters (\\t)\n\nFor example:\nPatientID\n12345\n67890\n\nFirstName\nJohn\nJane\n\nLastName\nDoe\nSmith\n\nDOB\nGender\n1985-04-15 Male\n1990-09-30 Female\n\n\fSupported Resources\nSummitEHR supports EXI export of the following patient resources:\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\nAllergies\nAppointment No navigation was required.\n\n```bash\n# Step 1: Probe the URL\ncurl -sI -L \"https://static1.squarespace.com/static/692e09ea4112f840c4fb54d8/t/69307ee493279950e0b33148/1764785893013/EHI+Export+Documentation+-+SummitEHR+v1.0.pdf\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n# Result: HTTP 200, Content-Type: application/pdf, 377,490 bytes\n\n# Step 2: Download the PDF\ncurl -sL \"https://static1.squarespace.com/static/692e09ea4112f840c4fb54d8/t/69307ee493279950e0b33148/1764785893013/EHI+Export+Documentation+-+SummitEHR+v1.0.pdf\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o downloads/EHI-Export-Documentation-SummitEHR-v1.0.pdf\n# Verified: `file` confirms PDF document, 4 pages\n\n# Step 3: Check the ONC certification page for additional documentation\ncurl -sL \"https://www.summitehr.com/onc-certification\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o /tmp/summitehr-onc.html\n# Found 4 PDF links on the page:\n#   - Pricing-Disclosures-SummitEHR-v10.pdf (not EHI-related)\n#   - Multi-factor-Authentication-Use-Cases-SummitEHR-v10.pdf (not EHI-related)\n#   - EHI-Export-Documentation-SummitEHR-v10.pdf (same PDF, short URL alias)\n#   - Application-Access-API-Guide-SummitEHR-v10.pdf (g)(9) API guide, not EHI export)\n# No additional EHI export documentation found.\n```\n\nThe certification page has an \"EHI Export Documentation\" section that provides a brief summary (identical to the PDF's introduction) and links to the same PDF. No additional data dictionaries, schemas, sample files, or supplemental documentation exist.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe entire EHI export documentation consists of a single 4-page PDF:\n\n**Page 1**: Cover page with DataQ Health logo, title \"EHI Export Documentation\", product name \"SummitEHR (v1.0)\".\n\n**Page 2**: Description of the export format:\n- Exports are in **TSV (Tab-Separated Values)** format\n- The EHI Export feature supports **single-patient** or **full practice population** export\n- For bulk/population exports, a **separate TSV file is generated for each resource type**\n- Each row in a resource file represents one patient's data\n- Includes a brief TSV example showing PatientID, FirstName, LastName, DOB, Gender columns\n- Lists programs that can open TSV files (Excel, Google Sheets, Notepad, Python/R)\n\n**Pages 3-4**: A bulleted list of 47 \"Supported Resources\" — the resource types available for export:\n\nAllergies, Appointment reminders, Appointments, Assessments, Care plans, Cognitive statuses, Diet, Document Details, Encounter built procedures, Encounters, Exam, Family history, Family history diseases, Follow up appointments, Functional statuses, Goals, Immunizations, Implantable devices, Interventions, Lab order diagnosis, Lab Orders, Lab test result notes, Lab test results, Lab tests, Medications, Past medical history, Past surgeries, Patient addresses, Patient care team members, Patient contacts, Patient information, Patient insurances, Patient payments, Patient races, Patient tasks, Patient vitals, PHQ 9 screening, Pregnancy status, Prior authentication, Problems, Progress notes, Related person details, SDOH, Smoking status, Social history, Unsigned documents, Vaping status.\n\nThe PDF contains **no embedded URLs**, **no attachments**, and **no links to additional resources**. The PDF metadata shows it was authored by \"Abdur Rehman\" and created on December 3, 2025, converted from a Word document via \"Microsoft: Print To PDF.\"\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nThe 47 resource types listed in the documentation suggest that summitEHR has attempted a genuine (b)(10) export — this is not merely a FHIR (g)(10) repackaging. The resource list goes well beyond USCDI/US Core, including several data types that would not be found in a standard FHIR API:\n\n**Clearly covered domains:**\n- **Demographics**: Patient information, Patient addresses, Patient contacts, Patient races\n- **Problems/Diagnoses**: Problems\n- **Medications**: Medications\n- **Allergies**: Allergies\n- **Lab data**: Lab Orders, Lab order diagnosis, Lab tests, Lab test results, Lab test result notes\n- **Vitals**: Patient vitals\n- **Immunizations**: Immunizations\n- **Implantable devices**: Implantable devices\n- **Family history**: Family history, Family history diseases\n- **Clinical notes**: Progress notes, Unsigned documents\n- **Care plans**: Care plans, Goals, Interventions\n- **Encounters**: Encounters, Encounter built procedures, Exam\n- **Social determinants**: SDOH, Social history, Smoking status, Vaping status\n- **Behavioral/screening**: PHQ 9 screening, Assessments, Cognitive statuses, Functional statuses\n- **Insurance**: Patient insurances\n- **Payments**: Patient payments\n- **Scheduling**: Appointments, Appointment reminders, Follow up appointments\n- **Care team**: Patient care team members, Related person details\n- **Other clinical**: Diet, Pregnancy status, Past medical history, Past surgeries, Prior authentication, Document Details, Patient tasks\n\n**Potential gaps or unclear areas:**\n- **Prescriptions/e-prescribing data**: \"Medications\" is listed but there's no separate resource for prescription orders, refill history, pharmacy routing data, or controlled substance prescriptions (EPCS). Given the NewCrop integration for e-prescribing, this data may be in the \"Medications\" resource, but it's unclear.\n- **Billing/claims detail**: \"Patient payments\" and \"Patient insurances\" are present, which is encouraging. However, there's no resource for charges, claims, billing codes, or superbills. The product research was unclear on whether summitEHR has integrated billing; if it does, the export may be missing billing detail.\n- **Referrals**: No resource for referral orders or referral tracking.\n- **Telehealth session data**: The product supports telehealth, but no resource specifically covers telehealth encounters or session records (these may be captured under \"Encounters\").\n- **Patient portal messages / Secure messaging**: Not listed as a resource type, despite the product supporting secure messaging.\n- **Direct messages**: Not listed, though the product is certified for Direct messaging (h)(1).\n- **Clinical quality measure data**: Not listed as a resource, though the product is certified for CQM (c)(1)-(c)(3).\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses **TSV (Tab-Separated Values)** — a simple, non-standard but highly portable flat-file format. This is a reasonable choice for a (b)(10) export:\n\n- TSV is easy to parse and process with any programming language or spreadsheet tool\n- One file per resource type is a clean organizational model\n- Each row represents one patient, which is simple but potentially limiting for resources with one-to-many relationships (e.g., a patient with multiple allergies — it's unclear whether multiple allergies produce multiple rows or are concatenated into one row)\n\n**Critical limitation**: There is no documentation whatsoever of the **columns/fields** in each TSV file. The documentation provides a single trivial example (PatientID, FirstName, LastName, DOB, Gender) but does not define:\n- What columns appear in each of the 47 resource files\n- Data types for each column\n- Value sets or coded values\n- How relationships between resources are expressed (foreign keys, patient identifiers)\n- How multi-valued fields are handled\n- Date/time formats\n- How null/empty values are represented\n- Character encoding\n\nWithout field-level documentation, a recipient of the export would have to reverse-engineer the meaning of each column from the data itself. This is a significant gap.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe documentation is **extremely minimal**. At 4 pages (with one being a cover page and one being mostly blank), this is among the thinnest EHI export documentation possible:\n\n- **No data dictionary**: Just a list of 47 resource names with no field definitions\n- **No schema**: No TSV header definitions, no JSON schema, no formal specification\n- **No sample data**: Only a trivial example of a patient demographics snippet\n- **No export instructions**: Only says the feature \"lets you manually export\" — no screenshots, no step-by-step walkthrough, no explanation of where to find the feature in the UI\n- **No worked examples**: No real-world sample export files\n- **No versioning/changelog**: Only the v1.0 designation\n\nA developer receiving this export would know they're getting TSV files for 47 resource types, but would have no guidance on interpreting the data beyond column headers in the files themselves.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity**: Resource-name level only. No field-level documentation at all.\n- **Coded fields**: Not documented. No value sets specified.\n- **Relationships**: Not documented. No description of how to link data across the 47 resource files.\n- **Data types**: Not specified.\n- **Versioning**: v1.0 only, no change history.\n\nThe documentation reads like a compliance checkbox — a minimal document created to satisfy the (b)(10) certification requirement. The list of 47 resources suggests the vendor has thought about which data to include, but the total absence of field-level documentation makes the export effectively opaque to anyone who doesn't already have access to the system.\n\n### Overall Assessment\n\nsummitEHR's EHI export approach has a **promising scope** — the 47 resource types cover most of the clinical data domains you'd expect from an ambulatory EHR, plus insurance and payment data. The use of TSV rather than FHIR suggests this is a genuine (b)(10) effort, not a (g)(10) repackaging.\n\nHowever, the documentation is **critically incomplete**. A list of resource names without field definitions is barely better than no documentation at all. The product was certified very recently (August 2025, with the PDF created December 2025), and this appears to be a v1.0 startup EHR with minimal documentation infrastructure. The quality of the documentation may improve over time, but as it stands, a data recipient would need the actual export files to understand what's in them.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://static1.squarespace.com/static/692e09ea4112f840c4fb54d8/t/69307ee493279950e0b33148/1764785893013/EHI+Export+Documentation+-+SummitEHR+v1.0.pdf\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\nNone.
